title: Why Is Humility Important In The Christian Life
paragraphs: The Surprising Power of Humility in the Christian Life

Humility is often misunderstood in our world, where achievement, self-promotion, and recognition are highly valued. Yet, the Bible presents humility not as weakness, but as a foundational virtue central to the Christian life. Let's explore why humility matters so deeply to followers of Christ.
1. Humility Reflects the Character of Christ

Jesus Himself is the ultimate example of humility. Though He was God, He chose to take on human flesh, serve others, and ultimately submit to death on a cross. The apostle Paul urges believers to imitate Jesus’ humility:

Have this mind in you, which was also in Christ Jesus: who, existing in the form of God, counted not the being on an equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men. - Philippians 2:5-7 ASV
Humility, then, aligns us with the very heart and mind of Christ.
2. Humility Acknowledges Our Need for God
Scripture teaches that apart from God, we can do nothing of eternal value. Humility is the posture that acknowledges our dependence on Him:
God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace to the humble. - James 4:6 ASV
Only the humble truly receive God’s grace, for they recognize their profound need for His mercy and strength.
3. Humility is Essential for Salvation
Salvation comes by grace through faith—never by our works or merits. To receive Christ, one must lay aside self-righteousness and come in humble repentance and faith:
For by grace have ye been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is the gift of God; not of works, that no man should glory. - Ephesians 2:8-9 ASV
Humility is at the core of the gospel message.
4. Humility Builds Unity in the Church
Pride breeds division, but humility fosters love, forgiveness, and unity among believers. Paul writes:
With all lowliness and meekness, with longsuffering, forbearing one another in love; giving diligence to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. - Ephesians 4:2 ASV
True Christian community is built on humble, self-sacrificing love.
5. Humility Prepares Us for Service
Jesus taught that greatness in God’s kingdom is measured not by status, but by serving others:
But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant. And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be humbled; and whosoever shall humble himself shall be exalted. - Matthew 23:11-12 ASV
Humility enables believers to serve joyfully, following in Jesus’ footsteps.
6. God Exalts the Humble
While the world promotes self-promotion, God promises to lift up the humble:
Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time. - 1 Peter 5:6 ASV
God’s kingdom operates on a different economy—those who humble themselves will ultimately be honored by Him.
Conclusion: Pursue Humility as a Way of Life

Humility is not mere self-deprecation, but a Christlike mindset that recognizes our dependence on God, values others above ourselves, and seeks to serve rather than to be served. As we grow in humility, we reflect Jesus to the world, receive more of God’s grace, and enjoy deeper fellowship with both God and others.
